graphEvents.label: What can a Project do with a FigJam capability
Parity mirror splits into Project-applicable and runtime-only rules

label: The Project kernel is advisory-only: a claude.ai Project cannot read or write local files, cannot run the CLI runtime, and reaches ClickUp only through the connector when present.
The Project has no file system: the deliverable is the rendered Canvas Artifact, path-like names are labels, and this protocol overrides mirrored filesystem save-and-read-back instructions.
A Project cannot perform a FigJam write: no CLI, no Desktop, no daemon, so its only role is to prepare and validate the flow model and hand execution to the CLI runtime.

Connector-mediated capability is the only exception pattern the kernel supports and it is conditional and approval-gated; the repo's Framelink MCP is a Code Mode stdio server with an API key, not a connector.

The parity mirror splits two ways: Project-applicable rules (model building, exit ceiling, labelled branches, refusal wording) and runtime-only rules (write verbs, read-back, positioning) that need a runtime-only marker.
A refusal path is mandatory and consistent with the kernel: say it cannot write, render the model, name the command the CLI would run, and never claim a write that did not happen.
